title: Good mock exponential map and factorization M × m^⊥_{x,0+} → MG_{x,0+}
body_html:
Good mock exponential map

Definition. Suppose $M \le G$, $\mathcal{B}(M) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{B}(G)$, and for $x \in \mathcal{B}(M)$ a continuous bijection $\mathrm{Exp} : \mathfrak{g}_{x, 0+} \to G_{x, 0+}$. We call $\mathrm{Exp}$ good if:

  • (a) $\mathrm{Exp}$ induces a group iso $\mathrm{Exp}r : \mathfrak{g}{x, r} / \mathfrak{g}{x, r+} \;\xrightarrow{\sim}\; G{x, r} / G_{x, r+}$;
  • (b) for $X \in \mathfrak{g}_{x, 0+}$, $H \in \mathfrak{g}_{x, r}$, $\mathrm{Exp}(X + H)\, \mathrm{Exp}(X)^{-1}\, G_{x, r+} = \mathrm{Exp}_r(H)$.

Examples

  • Cayley transform $C(X) = (1 + X/2)(1 - X/2)^{-1}$ is a good mock exponential for $G$ a classical group or general linear group with $p \ne 2$.
  • Truncated $\exp$ is a good mock exponential for general reductive $G$ when $p$ is sufficiently large (BCH-controlled).
  • In general the mock exponential exists once a pinning is fixed; see [Adler §1.5].

Factorization $\varphi_x$

Decompose $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{m} \oplus \mathfrak{m}^\perp$ as $M$-invariant subspaces under $\mathrm{Ad}$. With $\mathfrak{m}{x, r} := \mathfrak{g}{x, r} \cap \mathfrak{m}$ and the analogous $\mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, r}$, $\mathfrak{g}_{x, r} = \mathfrak{m}_{x, r} \oplus \mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, r}$.

Define $$\varphi_x : M \times \mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, 0+} \to G, \qquad (m, X) \mapsto m\, \mathrm{Exp}(X).$$

Proposition (Sheaf7 App A). $\varphi_x$ is injective and its image equals $M G_{x, 0+}$.

The proofs use the BCH/decomposition formula iteratively along the filtration $r_0 < r_1 < \cdots$.

Restriction to $K_x$ and gluing

Corollary. $\varphi_x$ restricts to a bijection $M_x \times \mathfrak{k}^\perp_{x, 0+} \to K_x$, where $\mathfrak{k}^\perp_{x, 0+} := \mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, 0+} \cap \mathfrak{k}_{x, 0+}$.

Theorem (apartment version). Fixing an apartment $A$ of $\mathcal{B}(M)$, the maps $\{\varphi_x\}_{x \in A}$ glue to a bijection $$\varphi : M \times \bigcup_{x \in A} \mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, 0+} > \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; M \bigcup_{x \in A} G_{x, 0+}.$$

The proof reduces to overlapping pairs and uses Iwahori decomposition [MP96 Thm 4.2] of $\widetilde G$ for an enveloping $(\widetilde G, \widetilde M, \Gamma)$ with $G = \widetilde G^\Gamma$, $M = \widetilde M^\Gamma$.

This apartment-wide factorization is the crucial input to [[node:depth_zero_reduction.M_K_orbit_bijection]].
